headline: Lehman Caves and Campground Reservations
reservation: Lehman Caves tours are the park's primary bottleneck and must be booked weeks or months in advance via Recreation.gov; walk-ins are rarely available. Developed campgrounds also require advance booking during the summer season. Always check the official NPS website for current cave tour schedules and road accessibility updates.

days.title: Subterranean Secrets

stops.name: Lehman Caves
stops.detail: Join a ranger-led tour to view rare marble formations like shields and soda straws.

stops.name: Lehman Creek Trail
stops.detail: Walk along the riparian corridor to see the transition from desert to mountain forest.

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes; the drive from Baker to the visitor center is short but steep.
days.note: Cave temperatures are a constant 52°F; a light jacket is suggested year-round.

days.title: Ancient Forests and Glaciers
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Lower Lehman Creek

stops.name: Bristlecone Pine Grove
stops.detail: Hike to see some of the oldest living trees on Earth, surviving for over 4,000 years.

stops.name: Wheeler Peak Glacier
stops.detail: Continue past the pines to see the only glacier in Nevada at the base of the peak.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive features steep grades and switchbacks.
days.note: The high elevation (above 10,000 feet) requires pacing and plenty of hydration.

days.title: High Desert Horizons
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Lehman Caves Visitor Center

stops.name: Mather Overlook
stops.detail: Stop for expansive views of the Great Basin's signature 'basin and range' topography.

stops.name: Stella Lake
stops.detail: Walk the Alpine Lakes Loop to see high-altitude water reflecting the Snake Range.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours; pullouts are frequent and worth the stop for photography.
days.note: Check for afternoon thunderstorms which are common at high altitudes during summer.

intel.title: Scenic Drive Limits
intel.text: Parking at the Wheeler Peak Trailhead is limited and fills early on summer weekends. Consider mid-week visits to ensure access to the highest trails.

intel.title: Remote Desert Hazards
intel.text: Cellular service is virtually non-existent within the park and extremely limited in Baker. Ensure you have a full tank of gas and physical maps before entering the Snake Range.

intel.title: Limited Supply Points
intel.text: Baker is the only nearby source for fuel, and services can be seasonal. The nearest major hubs are Ely, Nevada, or Delta, Utah, both over 60 miles away.

intel.title: High Altitude Access
intel.text: Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive usually opens in late June and closes with the first heavy snow in October. Always check the official road status before planning a summit hike.

intel.title: Dark Sky Compliance
intel.text: As an International Dark Sky Park, visitors are encouraged to use red-light flashlights at night. Stargazing programs are popular; check the visitor center for seasonal schedules.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental in Cedar City or Ely and buy all necessary groceries and supplies before the long drive to Baker. Confirm your cave tour time immediately upon arrival at the visitor center.
plan.vehicle: A reliable vehicle with good brakes is necessary for the 8% grades on Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive; large RVs are restricted on the upper sections.
plan.goldenHour: Mather Overlook provides a wide perspective for watching the desert floor transition into twilight, with mountains casting long shadows across the basin.
